summary: Author a state machine as a node graph asset, then drive it at runtime with one component.
overview: A state machine you draw rather than write. States, transitions, conditions and parameters live in an asset with no scene dependency; a runner component builds a real StateMachine from it at runtime and binds each node to a component that implements IState.
The split is the point: the graph is data a designer can edit, and the behaviour behind each node is ordinary code.

features.name: Runner
features.what: the component you put in a scene. Builds and drives the machine from an asset.

features.name: Graph asset
features.what: the reusable definition — states, transitions and parameters, no scene references.

features.name: Graph data
features.what: the nodes, transitions, conditions and parameters the asset is made of.

features.name: Graph editor
features.what: the node canvas: drag nodes, connect transitions, edit conditions.

useCases: Enemy behaviour a designer can retune without a programmer.
Game flow — lobby, countdown, playing, round over — authored visually.
Reusing one behaviour graph across several enemy types.

walkthrough.name: Asset
walkthrough.what: The graph this runner drives. Several runners can share one asset.

walkthrough.name: Node binding
walkthrough.what: Each graph node resolves to a component implementing IState. A node bound to a component that does not implement it logs a warning and does nothing.

walkthrough.name: Parameters
walkthrough.what: Named values transitions test against, in the same spirit as Animator parameters.

walkthrough.name: Conditions
walkthrough.what: All clauses on a transition must pass, matching the Animator's AND default.

gotchas.title: The graph is shared, the state is not
gotchas.body: Two runners on one asset each build their own machine. Editing the asset changes both; runtime state stays per runner.

gotchas.title: A node needs a bound component that implements IState
gotchas.body: Otherwise the node exists in the graph and does nothing at runtime, with only a warning to say so.

gotchas.title: A MonoBehaviour state still has its own Update
gotchas.body: Unity keeps calling it independently of the machine. Put per-frame work in Tick only, or it runs twice.
